memory_update.text: AMKR is the cleanest US-listed OSAT candidate for the AI advanced-packaging/HBM-backend capacity node; it should remain in later layers if AI/HPC advanced-packaging revenue mix and utilization evidence strengthen.

KLIC is a lower-attention equipment candidate tied to bonding and 2.5D/3D packaging transitions; survival depends on verifying HBM-system shipments, backlog, and advanced-solutions revenue materiality.
FORM maps to the HBM test/probe-card gate rather than OSAT capacity directly; useful for the testing/certification bottleneck lane.

The node should be split in later layers into OSAT capacity, advanced-packaging equipment, HBM wafer/probe test, inspection/metrology, substrates/interconnect, and packaging materials because each has different evidence and cycle risk.
US-listed coverage is thin for pure-play memory backend and fan-out panel-level packaging; important non-US names such as Powertech may be more direct but were excluded from this US-listed pass.

node: Advanced packaging, HBM backend, memory packaging/test, fan-out panel-level packaging, and OSAT capacity
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the AI advanced-packaging/HBM-backend OSAT node found one reference anchor and three US-listed underfollowed or less-obvious public-market mappings. TSM remains the context anchor for CoWoS/InFO/SoIC demand and bottleneck framing. The discovery lane points to Amkor as the most direct US-listed OSAT exposure, Kulicke & Soffa as an advanced-packaging bonder/equipment supplier tied to HBM and 2.5D/3D transitions, and FormFactor as a probe-card/test-gate supplier whose HBM demand is explicitly linked to generative AI. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
